subject: Lyra Health — HIPAA onboarding evidence & BAA timeline
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@lyrahealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lyra Health Security Team <security@lyrahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:07:00 -0500
Subject: Lyra Health — HIPAA onboarding evidence request and BAA timeline

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Lyra is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Our legal and security teams are starting a short onboarding RFP focused on HIPAA readiness so we can scope a pilot that will process PHI (therapy notes metadata). The ask is two-fold:

1) Evidence pack: flow diagrams, locations of PHI at rest, encryption configs (KMS), key rotation cadence, SOC 2 report (redacted), and a list of relevant controls mapped to our questionnaire (we attached Appendix A).
2) BAA: a draft or standard sample we can share with our legal counsel; if there are common redlines, flag them up front.

Requested timeline: we need an initial evidence delivery by EOD Nov 30 to keep our procurement window. Can you advise on feasibility and a point of contact for technical follow-ups? We may also request a short walkthrough for our security engineers.

Attachments: Lyra_RFP_HIPAA_AppendixA.pdf (questionnaire)

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Senior Security Program Manager
Lyra Health

---
Note: Lyra will share a short set of sample prompts that will touch PHI; we will need to understand token handling and retention behavior for those flows.
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>

Team — forwarding Lyra's note (see attachment). They want a targeted evidence pack + draft BAA by EOD Nov 30 (US Eastern). Can we hit a safe, defensible deliverable? Specific asks below:

- Monica: can you produce a short evidence pack (dataflow diagram, encryption/key mgmt, retention table) and a SOC 2 redacted statement? I know there are SOC artifacts in the security drive.
- Marissa: please coordinate legal/draft BAA and flag any standard exceptions we expect from enterprise counsel.
- Karthik: can your onboarding team confirm the PHI handling model for the pilot (storage, temp caching, KV cache behavior) and recommended configuration (dedicated vs hosted)? Also indicate if we need a Private deployment for the pilot.
- Vivek: please review the list for any open compliance gaps; priority is not promising anything we can't evidence in 5 business days.

Proposed plan:
- Today (Nov 25): triage questionnaire and assign owners (this email).
- Nov 26–29: produce artifacts and internal review.
- Nov 30 AM (PST): draft BAA and evidence pack sent to Emily; offer a Dec 1 technical walkthrough.

I will own the customer comms. Monica — attaching Lyra_RFP_HIPAA_AppendixA.pdf from their email.

Thanks,
Maya
Director, Solutions Engineering

Subject: Re: Lyra Health — HIPAA onboarding evidence request and BAA timeline

Maya — we can meet the Nov 30 target with a scoped delivery. High-level plan and artifacts I'll produce by Nov 29 EOD PST:

1) RI_PHIdataflow_diagram_v1.pdf — sequence diagrams showing request path (hosted API) and optional Dedicated flow; annotation for where PHI may appear (prompt text, generated outputs, ephemeral KV cache).
2) Encryption & Key Management summary — KMS provider(s), key rotation cadence, CMEK options for Private/Dedicated, TLS in transit.
3) Retention table (how long prompts, responses, and logs are kept per deployment mode, with recommended settings for pilot).
4) SOC 2 redacted summary + control mapping to Lyra Appendix A (we will provide a mapping doc).
5) RI_Security_Evidence_Pack.zip — contains sample config snippets and our standard ops checklist.

Open items we need input on before finalizing:
- Karthik: please confirm whether Lyra will require Dedicated capacity for pilot (legal sometimes insists). If yes, we need to include estimated lead time and whether we can offer a short-term reserved instance.
- Marissa: I'll hand over the BAA draft; please include typical enterprise redlines we escalate for legal.
- Vivek: any showstoppers on encryption boundaries?

I'll attach the artifacts to my email to Emily on Nov 30 AM PST and propose a Dec 1 11:00 AM ET walkthrough (45 mins).

-Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Attached is a scoped evidence bundle and a draft BAA to start the legal conversation. High-level notes:

- Evidence delivered: RI_PHIdataflow_diagram_v1.pdf (annotated flows), RI_Security_Evidence_Pack.zip (controls and redacted SOC 2 section), and an encryption summary. See attached list.
- BAA: RI_Draft_BAA_20261130.pdf attached. This is our standard BAA for hosted pilots; it includes the common security and breach notification language. Marissa and our legal team will be available to review redlines.
- Pilot recommendation: for the narrow set of prompts Lyra described (therapy-session metadata, limited PII), Hosted with dedicated customer routing and strict retention controls will meet requirements for a short pilot. If Lyra prefers explicit tenant isolation we can stand up Dedicated capacity — Karthik is preparing lead-time estimates and a cost delta.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review attached artifacts and BAA with your counsel.
2) Schedule a technical walkthrough: Dec 1, 11:00 AM ET (45 mins). Monica will lead and Karthik will join for deployment options.
3) If legal requests a different BAA posture (Private/on-prem), we'll set expectation on timeline — that route typically needs 6–8 weeks.

DocuSign placeholder for BAA: https://docusign.com/placeholder/LYR-BAA-20261130
Internal drive for evidence: https://redwood.app/internal/drive/RI_SEC/LYR-2026-ONBOARDING (internal link, view-permission required)

Attachments: RI_Draft_BAA_20261130.pdf, RI_PHIdataflow_diagram_v1.pdf, RI_Security_Evidence_Pack.zip

Looking forward to the walkthrough. Let me know if you need anything earlier.
